To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amount of unintegrate HIV-1 DNA (HIV-uDNA) in the PBMCs of HIV-infected asymptomatic patients who are not on therapy is much higher than the amount of HIV-uDNA in the PBMC of HIV-infected patients who are on nucleoside antiviral therapy.

a significant amount (approximately 50-60%) of human immunodeficiency (HIV) viral DNA in asymptomatic HIV-infected patients who have never received antiretrovirus therapy is in the form of unintegrated HIV DNA, and that the level of unintegrated HIV viral DNA is significantly decreased by antiretrovial therapy with nucleoside analogs.

asymptomatic HIV infected individuals who are not on therapy have a significant amount of unintegrated HIV DNA in their PBMCs and that this amount is reduced to a very low level by nucleoside antiviral therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of human immunodeficiency type 1 (HIV-1) DNA in peripheral blood mononucleated cells (PBMC).
the development of new markers of the efficacy of nucleoside therapy in asymptomatic HIV-1-infected patients.
the quantitation of unintegrated human immune virus DNA in asymptomatic individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the presence of a normal immune system (as measured by CD4 counts above 400) there is a significant amount of unintegrated HIV DNA in PBMCs of patients not on therapy, which can be reduced by therapy.
the amount of unintegrate HIV-1 DNA was significantly lower in asymptomatic patients who had received antiretrovirus therapy for at least 2 months.
in patients with HIV infection, there is a significant amount of unintegrated HIV DNA present in their PBMCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amount of unintegrate HIV DNA in PBMCs is significantly lower in asymptomatic patients who are on antiretrovial therapy than in those who are not.
a significant amount (50-60%) of the total HIV DNA is in the unintegrate form.
HIV-1 DNA is present in the form of unintegrated viral genomes in asymptomatic HIV-1 seropositive patients, and that the level of this DNA is reduced by nucleoside therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of unintegrating HIV DNA in PBMCs is a marker of the efficacy and potency of antiretrovirally therapy.

the presence of a significant amount of unintegrated HIV DNA in asymptomatic, healthy patients is a new marker of HIV replication in vivo, and that nucleoside antivirals reduce the amount of unintegrate HIV DNA in PBMCs.
the amount of unintegrate HIV DNA (HIV-uDNA) in the PBMCs of asymptomatic patients on therapy is much lower than in patients not on therapy.
